source.title: Cross-Architecture Steering Transfer in Language Models: A Systematic Empirical Study

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representational alignment and its relationship to model scale using SAE features, MNN matching, Pearson correlation, and Procrustes alignment, rather than reproducing the original study's method. It also tests whether cross-model mappings support steering transfer.
record.gate_note: The paper reports geometric alignment, feature matching, and cross-model steering outcomes. Rows record scale-tier alignment, raw-activation alignment, domain-level alignment, and steering transfer. Results cited from prior work are not included. The paper also reports pair-specific B2 results and prompt-sensitivity analyses; detailed pair-level B2 rows and individual prompt rows are not extracted because the scale-tier and domain summaries capture the main alignment outcomes within the row limit.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-architecture SAE-feature alignment (MNN plus Pearson validation) and raw-activation CCA+Procrustes alignment across five LLMs of 0.8B–8B. It compares these by scale tier and domain, and tests whether mapped representations support steering in another model. These are different methods aimed at whether representations converge with scale (V1), are mappable (V4), share features (V5), depend on metric and inputs (V6), and converge only partially (V7). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim feature-level universality at ≥1.7B and that GPT-2's weaker alignment reflects SAE resolution rather than geometry, since raw Procrustes stays high. They present this as the first functional complement to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. They call the 1.7B threshold suggestive (n=1 per tier) and the B3-TI advantage over native not significant (p=0.14).
record.recipe_differences: Uses per-model TopK SAEs, MNN feature matching, Pearson and Procrustes validation, and MLP bridges or a shared concept space to test cross-model alignment and steering. It does not reproduce the original study's measurement recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment results vary substantially by semantic domain and by measure: raw-activation Procrustes cosines are high even where SAE feature-pair pass rates are lower. Steering results also depend on model, prompt, and injection strength; DeepSeek and GPT-2 have restricted strength ranges due to repetition instability.

fits_no_version.finding: B3-TI steering vectors show bidirectional control: median |Δ−|/|Δ+| 1.71, with 82% of pairs ≥0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model transferred steering directions act bidirectionally on the target concept.

fits_no_version.finding: The instruction-tuned Hermes-LLaMA's pass rates (42.6–47.7%) are within 2pp of base-model pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SFT does not disrupt cross-model representational alignment.

record.problems: Only five models and two architectural lineages are tested; there is one model per tier below 7B, so the proposed scale threshold is not a systematic scaling law. All models share the same corpus, and a disjoint-corpus ablation is deferred. The raw-space Procrustes values are described as optimized upper bounds. DeepSeek results are restricted by generation instability, and the B3-TI aggregate advantage over native vectors is not statistically significant (p=0.14). The study uses one residual-stream layer and does not provide mechanistic activation-patching evidence.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed directed-pair B2 values in Table 11 are summarized by the scale-tier results in R1–R4; pair-specific CCA/Procrustes values in Table 3 are not separately extracted. Individual prompt-level results in Table 23 and figures are omitted. The paper also reports C3-EncDec model-level win rates in Table 5; only its aggregate result and geometry explanation are retained in R42.

untested.parts: Modalities beyond text; architectures beyond GPT-2/LLaMA lineages; more than one model per tier below 7B. Scale is confounded with positional encoding (GPT-2 is the only absolute-PE model). No capability measure.
Entire version: no vision or image–caption data.
Entire version: no same-architecture different-seed comparison (all SAEs use seed 42; models differ).
Plain linear maps as steering transfer, layer stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping. The bridge is a 67M-parameter MLP.
Neighbour-count settings for mutual-kNN-style metrics; out-of-distribution inputs.
Whether shared data or objectives cause alignment: all models use the same corpus, and the disjoint-corpus ablation is deferred. A plateau over a broad scale sweep.

missing.what: Naive zero-projection baseline win rate 65.7% (per model 16.7/80.0/70.0/71.7/90.0). Much of the cross-model win rate is reachable without a learned map.
Extraction-method dependence: Hungarian Run 1 gives a 68.4% pass rate (GPT-2 cross-scale 65–79%) vs MNN Run 2 45.5%. The scale gap appears only under MNN.
For GPT-2-large as target, SAE-free Procrustes 0.87 vs B2 pair cosine 0.72.
Pooled validated-pair stats: mean Pearson r 0.512 (median 0.545); enrichment 28.6× over permutation null.
Universal concept coverage: 46/107 raw clusters span all 5 models; 11 canonical concepts with 5/5 coverage after human merging.
Δ at fixed s=1 averages about zero for all methods (B3-TI −0.004, native 0.000).
LLM-judge win rates are low (B3-TI 28.3%, C3-Dec 38.0% on qualifying prompts) and uncorrelated with DeBERTa Δ (r=−0.004).

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint. Win rates take the best of several positive strengths, so 50% understates chance and inflates all win rates. The study's results bear on V4 mainly through steering transfer via a 67M MLP bridge, plus linear CCA+Procrustes. The reader's V6 label was limits_scope; the results actually support V6 (a challenge version), so it is relabelled supports. The reader's 'challenges' for DeepSeek C3-Dec was dropped because the failure is confounded by repetition collapse that also affects native vectors. Scale is confounded with absolute vs rotary position encoding (GPT-2 is the only absolute-PE model). Table 5 and the text disagree on DeepSeek's s=1 B3-TI rate (21.7% vs 30.0%).

versions.untested_parts: Does not test multiple modalities, broad architecture families, a systematic scaling law, or alignment against independently measured model capability. There is only one model per tier below 7B.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations.
Tests MLP bridges and shared-space steering vectors, not linear maps, layer stitching, relative representations, or unpaired-data mappings.
Tests SAE-feature correspondences and shared semantic concepts, not recurring individual neurons or circuits. The SAE features are not evidence that the same units or bases recur.
Compares several alignment metrics and domains, but does not systematically vary metric settings such as neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs. All models use the same corpus.

Reports incomplete alignment and shared-corpus use, but does not test whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment; the disjoint-corpus ablation is deferred. Does not establish a plateau across a broad scale sweep.
